illustrations.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create a NEW interior illustration for Vasyl Vyhovsky's private science-fiction diary "Повстання Мюридів", universe Дике Поле.
Reference image 1 is STYLE ONLY: match its exact warm off-white paper, monochrome graphite, pencil pressure variation, loose crosshatching, faint construction lines, restrained dark accents, softened smudges, and unfinished edges dissolving into paper. Do not copy its oak trees, park, or window composition.
Landscape 3:2 book vignette, generous pale margins. A capable but unpolished observational sketch drawn by a soldier from memory, with emotional attention to selected details and lightly sketched surroundings. No photographic rendering, ink wash, watercolor, glossy digital shading, or colored elements. The artwork itself fills the image: no book mockup, hands holding a pencil, desk surrounding a page, page curl, captions, writing, signature, watermark, collage, or panels.
Faction constraints: no blue-and-yellow flags or paired bands, no modern Ukrainian coat of arms, no generic three-arrow-fork insignia. No decorative rushnyky, embroidered towels, kushaks, sashes, embroidered waist belts, tassels, or hanging decorative cloth on combat gear. Functional equipment only.

Scene: station tavern during the diary entry of 11 October, with artificial gravity. First-person view from the narrator's place at a plain table. Across the table sit THREE veteran Sich Riflemen squad leaders in ordinary practical shipboard clothing, not power armor. Normal human proportions and different faces: a lean middle-aged man with short hair and a small moustache, a broad-faced older clean-shaven man, and a younger wiry man with close-cropped hair. They look like ordinary tired men at ease, yet their eyes remain watchful and unnervingly alert. One speaks quietly, one holds a plain metal cup, one listens with forearms on the table. Make natural hands anatomically credible.
A few cups and simple plates on the table. Subtle spaceship context in lightly drawn bulkhead ribs, a ventilation grille and recessed utility lighting behind them. No fantasy medieval tavern, no rustic costumes, no superhuman muscles, no combat action, no theatrical menacing poses, no insignia. Intimate seated eye-level view, faces and hands more detailed, table and station fade into loose pencil lines. A human moment before a dangerous mission.

Scene: diary entry 12 October, meeting TWO secretive kharakternyky in a transit corridor on a warp-transfer space station. First-person view of two ordinary-looking adult men stopped a few paces away, one slightly nearer than the other. Frame them from head to just below knees, enough to see their gear. Plain practical station coveralls and compact respirators covering nose and mouth, bare heads, alert eyes; neither glamorous nor monstrous. Their faces differ. Small utilitarian belt mounts carry a PAIR of compact straight sheathed Caucasian-kindjal-inspired daggers at each man's side, restrained plain handles and sheaths, no ornate ornament or oversized fantasy blades.
A few loosely indicated travelers pass farther behind them; industrial hatch ribs, conduits and a plain overhead light suggest an unremarkable space station. Focus the careful pencil work on eyes, respirators and the unusual daggers. Everything else sparse, tentative and unfinished. Their calm stillness against routine transit is the source of tension. No robes, cloaks, hoods, religious costume, glowing eyes, magic, owl/salamander helmets, armor, badges, banners or visible text.

Scene: quiet cabin before the warp jump in the entry of 15 October. Still life sketched by the narrator from his bunk: his newly issued heavy sealed powered infantry armor mounted EMPTY on a simple narrow maintenance support against a cabin wall, with its detached helmet and a gently curved chychuha SABER resting on an adjacent utilitarian bench. The armor has thick functional overlapping plates, powered joints, life-support fittings, substantial but believable proportions, restrained silver metal inlays represented only through pencil shading; no cloth decoration. It is a suit for a human, not a robot character or medieval knight.
Helmet shown in rear three-quarter view so its rear metal princely mark is visible. Reproduce ONLY the central mark from reference 2: TWO broad upward prongs forming a deep U-shaped notch, a tapered downward stem, and a SMALL SEPARATE CROSS above it. Render the insignia as a small subdued metal applique in graphite. Omit the blue oval, colored border, dotted ring, all colors; do NOT turn it into a modern trident, three-pronged fork or arrows. No other insignia elsewhere.
The saber has a slender gently curved blade, a short simple crossguard and a compact capped grip with an inactive small plasma pommel fitting; tasteful metal fittings, no glow, no giant fantasy blade, no mace or staff. Cabin wall, support and empty bunk corner are only loosely suggested. Focus on armor and helmet weight and the contrast of important new equipment with a cramped ordinary cabin. No person present, no heroic pose, no skulls, no ornamental cloth, no text.
